newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Manila preparing law for clearer investment rules.
newsitem.headline: Manila preparing law for clearer investment rules.

text.p: Philippines lawmakers are preparing legislation to make the rules on bidding for projects in that country clearer, Philippine Foreign Secretary Domingo Siazon said on Friday.
He said the move followed a Philippine Supreme Court decision last month that rescinded the sale of the historic Manila Hotel to Malaysia's Renong Bhd.
The court ruled that the building on Manila Bay was part of the national heritage and should only be sold to Filipinos.

"President Ramos has suggested that we take certain measures to ensure that there is no repetition of the same incident in the future," Siazon told reporters after a meeting with his Malaysian counterpart, Abdullah Ahmad Badawi.
Siazon and Abdullah attend a meeting of foreign ministers of the seven Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) and their counterparts in the 15-member European Union (EU).
"Some of our legislators are in fact trying to introduce legislation now to make sure that the rules of the game are quite clear," Siazon said.
He said the Philippine government was filing an appeal on the court decision as it wants the bidding process to proceed.
Asked if Malaysia was satisfied with the Philippines' explanation, Siazon said: "On the official side, yes. But I think it's very hard to explain this to the businessmen."
A Malaysian official said Renong did not intend to appeal the decision because it would be "very difficult".

Abdullah said he was told that the Philippines private sector and its chambers of commerce were very unhappy with the decision, which could cause losses to the country at a time when it is trying to encourage foreign investors.

Siazon said on Thursday that the decision was particularly damaging because Manila needed US$5.0 billion annually for its infrastructure projects. Of that, the country could raise only $2.5 billion from official assistance extended by donor nations.
The verdict also was embarassing because Manila earlier had to convince Renong to take part in the bidding, Siazon said.

The ministers said in order to enhance economic relations, Malaysia and the Philippines should conclude at their next joint commission meeting in Kuala Lumpur several agreements on investment protection, double taxation and balance of payments.
ASEAN groups Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Phillipines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam.
